## GitHub Copilot's October 2 model cutover swaps Claude Opus 4.7's replacement to Opus 5.5

October 3, 2026 · by Pondero Newsdesk

GitHub's October 2 changelog confirmed the removal of Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7 from Copilot, pointing admins to Opus 5.5 instead of the Opus 5 named a month earlier.

# GitHub Copilot's October 2 model cutover swaps Claude Opus 4.7's replacement to Opus 5.5

GitHub finished a deprecation it announced a month ago, and the model it is steering admins toward has changed since that first notice. On September 3, GitHub told Copilot admins that Claude Opus 4.7 would retire October 2 in favor of Claude Opus 5. The October 2 changelog that actually carried out the cutover names a different target: Claude Opus 5.5.

## What happened

As of October 2, 2026, GitHub deprecated four models across every Copilot surface, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions, per the GitHub changelog. Both Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini 3.6 Flash give way to Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Kimi K2.7 Code hands off to Kimi K3. The fourth retirement carries the real change: Claude Opus 4.7's replacement is now Claude Opus 5.5, not the Claude Opus 5 that GitHub's September 3 notice had named a month earlier. GitHub said no admin action is required to remove the old models; they stay selectable in the Chat model picker without manual cleanup, just unsupported. Enterprise and Business admins who want the replacements available still have to turn them on through their organization's Copilot model policy before the new model shows up in the selector.

## Policies tuned for Opus 5 in September need a second look

Any admin who read the September notice literally and enabled Opus 5 specifically in their model policy has not actually provisioned the model GitHub now recommends. Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5, and GitHub added it to Copilot across every IDE surface on September 22, weeks after the original deprecation notice went out. The swap matters most for teams that locked workflows or Copilot Extensions to a named model string. Those integrations do not fail silently; they stop resolving once the underlying model is gone, so the fix is to re-check the model policy against today's changelog rather than the one from a month ago.

## What to watch next

Kimi K3 taking over as Copilot's suggested replacement for code-focused tasks lands in an awkward week for its maker. OpenAI disclosed on October 2 that it disrupted a reasoning-extraction campaign it ties to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, according to the report. GitHub has not said whether that dispute affects Kimi K3's standing inside Copilot, and nothing in the October 2 changelog suggests it will. Worth checking is whether GitHub's model-policy UI already lists Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 as available, or whether rollout lags the changelog entry for some tiers.

- Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated: GitHub changelog, October 2, 2026
- Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models: GitHub changelog, September 3, 2026
- OpenAI Disrupts Reasoning Extraction Campaign Linked to Moonshot AI Associates: The Hacker News, October 2, 2026

Author James Calloway

Date October 2, 2026

Stats 1 file changed, +680 insertions, −3 min read

# GitHub Copilot Deprecates Four Models Including Claude Opus 4.7

GitHub Copilot dropped Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7 as of October 2, 2026. Here's what to switch to and how admins enable replacements.

By James Calloway

## Changelog

- * Four models deprecated across all Copilot experiences as of October 2, 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7.
- * Suggested replacements are Gemini 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3, and Claude Opus 5.5.
- * Copilot Enterprise admins may need to enable alternative models via model policies in Copilot settings; no action is needed to remove deprecated models.

If your Copilot workflow leans on Claude Opus 4.7, Kimi K2.7 Code, or either of the recent Gemini Flash models, it's time to adjust. As of October 2, 2026, GitHub has deprecated four models across every Copilot surface — Chat, inline edits, ask mode, agent mode, and code completions. No partial rollout, no grace period mentioned in the announcement. The deprecation hits all experiences at once.

Here's the full list of what's gone and where GitHub points you next:

| Deprecated model | Deprecation date | Suggested alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini 3.5 Flash | 2026-10-02 | Gemini 3.8 Flash |
| Gemini 3.6 Flash | 2026-10-02 | Gemini 3.8 Flash |
| Kimi K2.7 Code | 2026-10-02 | Kimi K3 |
| Claude Opus 4.7 | 2026-10-02 | Claude Opus 5.5 |

The Gemini consolidation is the least surprising entry on the list. Two Flash generations collapsing into Gemini 3.8 Flash is standard fast-model churn — if you had automations pinned to 3.5 or 3.6, the migration path is a one-line change and, frankly, you were probably due for it anyway. The Kimi K2.7 Code to K3 jump follows the same pattern: a version bump, a newer model, move along.

Claude Opus 4.7 is the one that will sting some teams. Opus remains the go-to pick for developers who want maximum reasoning quality on hard refactors and gnarly agent tasks, and if you've tuned prompts or agent behavior around 4.7's output characteristics, you'll want to re-run your evals against Opus 5.5 before you assume parity. GitHub's suggested alternative is the direct successor, so the switch should be mechanical — but "should be" has burned plenty of teams before.

## What you actually need to do

For most users: update your workflows and integrations to call the supported models. That's it. GitHub states plainly that no action is required to remove the deprecated models — they simply stop being available.

Copilot Enterprise administrators have one extra step. Alternative models may need to be explicitly enabled through model policies in Copilot settings. The verification procedure GitHub describes:

1. Open your individual Copilot settings.
2. Confirm the policy is enabled for the specific model you want.
3. Check the Copilot Chat model selector in VS Code or on github.com — once the policy is live, the model appears there.

If a replacement model doesn't show up in the picker, the policy is the first thing to check. Don't file a bug report before you've ruled out your own admin config.

GitHub Enterprise customers with questions or concerns are encouraged to contact their account manager.

## Context worth having

Model churn at this pace is now the norm for Copilot. GitHub has been rotating third-party models in and out of the lineup on a steady cadence, and deprecations bundled like this — multiple vendors, single date, clear successor for each — look designed to keep the supported list tight rather than to strand anyone. The pattern also signals where the lineup is heading: newer Flash-tier models for speed-sensitive work like completions, and current-generation flagship models for chat, agent mode, and complex edits.

GitHub Retires Four Copilot Models While Claude Code Stable Lacks Fail-Closed Fixes · AIDevPulse

# GitHub Retires Four Copilot Models While Claude Code Stable Lacks Fail-Closed Fixes

3 Oct 2026

At a glance

- GitHub deprecated four Copilot models across all experiences on 2 Oct: Gemini 3.5 Flash and 3.6 Flash (to Gemini 3.8 Flash), Kimi K2.7 Code (to Kimi K3) and Claude Opus 4.7 (to Claude Opus 5.5).
- Claude Code v2.1.288 (npm 2:30 PM ET, GitHub 4:19 PM ET, 2 Oct) stops a dangerous `rm` inside `bash -c` or `sh -c` running unprompted in bypass mode or under a shell allow rule, and blocks PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks that could not be evaluated instead of skipping them.
- npm and the native installer still point `stable` at v2.1.285 while `latest` is v2.1.288, so a stable-channel fleet lacks both fixes.
- Smaller: a Copilot code review API with per-request effort, and computer use in public preview.

Today’s lead changes are quieter than a launch: four Copilot model ids are simply gone, and a Claude Code release makes permission checks fail closed where a check that could not run used to be skipped.

Treat today as the day you find the four retired names in your repos and enable the replacements in Copilot policy, confirm `claude --version` prints v2.1.288 wherever you use allow rules, hooks or bypass mode, and leave `/computer` off until someone owns it.

### 1. Four Copilot models are retired, and Kimi K3 needs an explicit switch

GitHub’s changelog says that as of 2 Oct 2026 these models are deprecated across all Copilot experiences, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and completions:

- Gemini 3.5 Flash is replaced by Gemini 3.8 Flash.
- Gemini 3.6 Flash is replaced by Gemini 3.8 Flash.
- Kimi K2.7 Code is replaced by Kimi K3.
- Claude Opus 4.7 is replaced by Claude Opus 5.5.

This executes a slate GitHub announced on 3 Sep, with one change: that notice named Claude Opus 5 as the Opus 4.7 alternative, and today’s names Opus 5.5. Today’s post says Enterprise administrators may need to enable the alternatives in model policy, and the 3 Sep one also named Business, so a Business admin should check too.

The enable step matters most for Kimi K3. GitHub’s supported-models page says open-weight models, Kimi K3 among them, are excluded from the default-availability policy and stay disabled until an admin turns them on, while GA models such as Opus 5.5 follow your default unless you configured them. GitHub’s pricing page lists Opus 5.5 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 output, and Kimi K3 at $3 and $15.

GitHub does not say what happens to a saved model choice or a workflow that names a retired model, so test that instead of assuming.

Practical dev impact: Search repos, prompt files and CI for the four names, and enable Kimi K3 in policy before anyone is pointed at it. Opus 4.7 to Opus 5.5 is a different model with its own price ($4 in, $20 out), so choose it on purpose. Another batch is scheduled for 19 Oct.

### 2. Claude Code v2.1.288 stops treating a check that could not run as a pass

Two fixes in the v2.1.288 notes change how permissions fail. First, a dangerous `rm`, such as one on `/` or the home directory, inside a `bash -c` or `sh -c` script used to run without a prompt in `bypassPermissions` mode or under a shell allow rule. The linked report (issue 96300, filed against v2.1.280 on Windows with Git Bash) explains why: the check looked for commands whose program is `rm`, and in `sh -c "rm -rf ..."` the program is `sh`. The reporter adds that no text check can cover every wrapper, since a script file or `python -c` gets past it, and the changelog names only `bash -c` and `sh -c`, so read the fix that narrowly.

Second, PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks were skipped when matching them failed or when the tool’s input could not be serialized to JSON, and now the call is blocked. That concerns the step that decides which hooks apply failing, or the tool’s input not converting to JSON, no

## GitHub Copilot deprecated models, October 2026: what to switch to and what it costs

Published October 2, 2026 · by Pondero Labs

The short version

Ten Copilot models retire on October 2 and October 19, 2026. Every retiring model mapped to GitHub's suggested swap, the per-token price change from GitHub's rate card, cheaper picks GitHub doesn't mention, and where old model names hide in your config.

Table of Contents

# GitHub Copilot deprecated models, October 2026: what to switch to and what it costs

Four GitHub Copilot models stopped working today. Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7 were deprecated across Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions on October 2, 2026 (GitHub Changelog, wave one), and six more go on October 19 (GitHub Changelog, wave two). GitHub names one suggested alternative per model and says nothing about price.

So we lined every swap up against GitHub's own per-token rate card (GitHub Docs, models and pricing). Four swaps get cheaper, four cost the same, and two cost more. Kimi K3 lists at more than three times Kimi K2.7 Code's input price, and GitHub's suggested replacement for GPT-5.4 costs more than two newer OpenAI models on the same page. Below: a per-model pick, the bill impact, and a one-line sweep for every place an old model name is still pinned.

## All ten retiring models, mapped

The class column is the label GitHub prints next to each model on its rate card (Lightweight, Versatile, Powerful), the only behavior signal GitHub publishes for these swaps.

| Retiring model | Gone on | GitHub's suggested swap | Class change on GitHub's rate card | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini 3.5 Flash | 2026-10-02 | Gemini 3.8 Flash | Lightweight to Versatile | Wave one, rates |
| Gemini 3.6 Flash | 2026-10-02 | Gemini 3.8 Flash | Versatile, unchanged | Wave one, rates |
| Kimi K2.7 Code | 2026-10-02 | Kimi K3 | Versatile to Powerful | Wave one, rates |
| Claude Opus 4.7 | 2026-10-02 | Claude Opus 5 | Powerful, unchanged | Wave one, rates |
| Gemini 3.7 Flash | 2026-10-19 | Gemini 3.8 Flash | Versatile, unchanged | Wave two, rates |
| GPT-5.5 | 2026-10-19 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Powerful, unchanged | Wave two, rates |
| GPT-5.4 | 2026-10-19 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Versatile to Powerful | Wave two, rates |
| GPT-5.4 mini | 2026-10-19 | GPT-5.6 Luna | Lightweight, unchanged | Wave two, rates |
| GPT-5 mini | 2026-10-19 | GPT-5.6 Luna | Lightweight, unchanged | Wave two, rates |
| Grok 4.5 | 2026-10-19 | Grok 4.6 | Versatile, unchanged | Wave two, rates |

Watch the GPT-5.4 and Kimi K2.7 Code rows. Both get bumped up a class, and both swaps raise the per-token price (GitHub Docs). Gemini 3.5 Flash also moves up a class, but its replacement is cheaper per token; everyone else stays put.

## What happens if you do nothing

Read GitHub's wording literally. Both notices say the models are deprecated "across all GitHub Copilot experiences," ask you to "update your workflows and integrations to use the supported models before this date," and add that "no action is required to remove the models after they have been deprecated" (wave one, wave two).

GitHub says nothing beyond that. Neither post says Copilot will quietly reroute a saved selection to the suggested alternative. GitHub cleans up its picker; anything on your side that names the old model by string is yours to fix. (Our September 8 news piece covered the wave-one announcement.)

## GitHub Copilot Drops Four Models on October 2, Including Claude Opus 4.7 and Two Gemini Flash Versions

September 8, 2026 · by Pondero Newsdesk

GitHub published a deprecation notice on September 3 listing four Copilot models that stop working across Chat, inline edits, agent mode, and code completions on October 2, 2026, with named replacements for each.

# GitHub Copilot Drops Four Models on October 2, Including Claude Opus 4.7 and Two Gemini Flash Versions

Four models will stop working across GitHub Copilot on October 2, 2026, and replacing them is not automatic. Admins who take no action before that date lose access without gaining the suggested alternatives.

## What

GitHub posted a deprecation notice on September 3, per the GitHub Changelog, listing the following models for retirement and their suggested replacements:

- Gemini 3.5 Flash, replaced by Gemini 3.8 Flash
- Gemini 3.6 Flash, replaced by Gemini 3.8 Flash
- Kimi K2.7 Code, replaced by Kimi K3
- Claude Opus 4.7, replaced by Claude Opus 5

All four will be removed from every Copilot surface on October 2: Chat, inline edits, ask mode, agent mode, and code completions. The scope covers both the GitHub.com web experience and IDE-connected Copilot sessions.

Replacement access is not automatic. Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business administrators must open their organization or enterprise Copilot settings, verify that each alternative model is listed, and confirm that the model policy enables it. Only after an admin enables the policy will users see the replacement model in the Copilot Chat model selector. After October 2, GitHub states no admin action is needed to remove the deprecated models; they will disappear from the selector without a manual cleanup step.

## Workflows pinned to deprecated models break on October 2

The October 2 deadline is four weeks out from the September 3 notice. Any Copilot agent mode workflow or Copilot Extension that calls a specific deprecated model by name will break at the cutover unless the integration is updated before then. Chat sessions where users pinned one of the four models in the selector will also lose that configuration without warning.

Teams running Copilot without an explicit model selection are less exposed; those sessions draw from the platform default rather than a named model. But organizations that standardized on Claude Opus 4.7 specifically for its reasoning characteristics, or on either Gemini Flash version for cost reasons, need to evaluate the replacements on their own workloads now. Claude Opus 5 is available in Copilot, per the GitHub Changelog, but admins need to confirm their tier includes it before the cutoff.

The three-step admin checklist: open Copilot settings at the org or enterprise level, enable the replacement model in the model policy, then have at least one developer confirm the model appears in the selector before October 2.

## What to watch next

GitHub has not confirmed whether the October 2 cutover applies equally to Copilot Workspace and Copilot Extensions-based integrations, which can bind to specific models through different configuration paths. The other thing to check before October 1: that Claude Opus 5 and Kimi K3 are available on your specific Copilot tier, since availability by tier was not detailed in the September 3 notice.

## Sources

- Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models: GitHub Changelog, September 3, 2026

# Claude not available in GitHub Copilot or Cursor? Why it’s missing from your model picker, and how to fix it

 Priya Sharma Oct 4 2026 - 09:30 UTC Updated Oct 13 2026 - 12:42 UTC 

The GitHub Copilot icon and Anthropic’s Claude spark. Image: GitHub (Copilot icon, Primer Octicons, MIT licence) and Anthropic (Claude spark)

Claude goes missing from GitHub Copilot’s model picker for one of four reasons: your plan doesn’t include that model, GitHub has retired it, your company hasn’t switched it on, or your editor is out of date. The most common is the first. GitHub’s supported models page shows that Claude Opus and Fable aren’t part of Copilot Pro at all, and that Opus 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7 have been retired since September. Cursor has a similar catch for one of its plans. Here’s how to work out which one you’ve hit, and what to do.

Jump to:

- Which Copilot plans include Claude?
- Claude Opus not available in GitHub Copilot Pro
- Claude Opus 4.6 or 4.7 missing from Copilot
- Claude not available in Copilot at work
- Claude not showing in VS Code, JetBrains or Xcode
- “Model not available” errors in Copilot
- Claude not available in Cursor
- FAQ

## Which GitHub Copilot plans include Claude?

Every paid Copilot plan includes some Claude models, but the top ones start at Copilot Pro+. GitHub’s plan table splits them like this:

| Claude model | Pro ($10) | Pro+ ($39) | Max ($100) | Business ($19/seat) | Enterprise ($39/seat) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Sonnet 5 and 5.5 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 | Annual plans only | Annual plans only | No | No | No |
| Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 | No | Yes | Yes | If an admin enables it | If an admin enables it |

Monthly prices in US dollars, from GitHub’s plans page. Business and Enterprise models also depend on your organisation’s settings (see below).

## Claude Opus not available in GitHub Copilot Pro

If you pay for Copilot Pro ($10 a month) and can’t find Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5 or Fable 5.1, nothing is broken: GitHub doesn’t include them in Pro. On Pro you can pick Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. To get Opus and Fable you need Copilot Pro+ ($39), Max ($100), or a Business or Enterprise seat.

Copilot Free and Copilot Student are more limited still. GitHub says both only get models through Auto, which picks a model for each request, so you can’t choose Claude by name at all.

## Claude Opus 4.6 or 4.7 missing from Copilot

GitHub retires older models on a schedule, and several Claude models have gone in the past five weeks. Its retirement history lists:

| Claude model | Retired from Copilot | GitHub’s suggested replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 4.7 | October 2, 2026 | Latest Claude Opus |
| Claude Opus 4.5 and 4.6 | September 1, 2026 | Latest Claude Opus |
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | September 1, 2026 | Latest Claude Sonnet |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 | September 1, 2026 (kept on annual Pro and Pro+) | Latest Claude Sonnet |
| Claude Opus 4.6 (fast mode) | June 29, 2026 | Latest Claude Opus in fast mode |
| Claude Sonnet 4 | May 1, 2026 | Latest Claude Sonnet |
| Claude Opus 4.1 | February 17, 2026 | Latest Claude Opus |

If a model you used every day vanished in early September or on October 2, this is almost certainly why, and switching back isn’t possible. The newest replacements are Claude Opus 5.5 (Pro+ and up) and Claude Sonnet 5.5, which is on every paid plan. Copilot may have quietly moved your chat to Auto when the old model went, so open the picker and choose the new one. These are GitHub’s dates: on Anthropic’s own API, Claude Sonnet 4.5 keeps working until November 30, 2026.

## Claude not available in Copilot at work (Business or Enterprise)

On a company plan, the models you see are decided by your organisation or enterp
